To determine the most optimal desorption conditions to minimize energy usage and cost, samples from a batch of PA-coated SBA-15 sorbents were subjected to a variety of temperature and vacuum pressures at various time lengths. Sorbents were tested by varying the temperature from 80-100oC, the vacuum pressure level from 0.2-0.3 bar, and the time length from 0.5 to 2 h. Sorbents were packed into a bed and fed air from the airlines in the lab overnight (~18 h) and once saturated, the beds were subjected to a combination of the listed desorption conditions. Following that, the sorbents were heated to 100oC with pure N flowing through the breakthrough system to 2 evaluate the residual CO on the sorbent. The data displayed in Figure 31 showed that the vacuum 2 desorption conditions that have been tested so far have successfully removed all the CO adsorbed 2 to the material under conditions of 0.2 bar vacuum, 100oC, and a desorption period of at least 37 min. When testing at lower temperatures and higher vacuum pressures (to minimize energy costs), no suitable conditions have been discovered yet for full CO removal. At 0.2 bar and 90oC, the 2 sorbent was only able to desorb 39% of the CO for 30 min or 66% for 1 h. At 0.3 bar and 100oC, the 2 sorbent was only able to desorb 55% of the CO for 30 min.
